properties.title: Special Weather Statement issued July 26 at 5:07AM EDT by NWS Wilmington NC
properties.description:
At 507 AM EDT, Doppler radar was tracking a cluster of strong
thunderstorms near Cades, or near Lake City, moving southeast at 30
mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 40 mph.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects.

This strong thunderstorm will be near...
Indiantown around 520 AM EDT.

Other locations impacted by this storm include Stuckey.
properties.instruction: If outdoors, consider seeking shelter inside a building.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued July 26 at 2:48AM EDT until July 26 at 6:00AM EDT by NWS Jackson KY
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Portions of east central and southeast Kentucky, including
the following counties, in east central Kentucky, Estill. In
southeast Kentucky, Jackson, Lee and Owsley.

* WHEN...Until 600 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 248 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain
have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are expected
over the area. This additional rain will result in minor
flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Arvel, Old Orchard, Wind Cave, New Zion, Lakes, Turkey Foot,
Earnestville, Banford, Wild Dog, Leighton, Alumbaugh, Drip
Rock, Cressmont, Delvinta, Travellers Rest, Ida May, Blanton
Flats, Wagersville, Vincent and Green Hall.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.
properties.area: Estill, KY; Jackson, KY; Lee, KY; Owsley, KY

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued July 26 at 1:48AM EDT until July 26 at 5:45AM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Central Cherokee County and northeastern Spartanburg County
in upstate South Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 545 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Ponding of water in urban or other areas is occurring or is
imminent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 148 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have
fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are expected over
the area. This additional rain is expected to lead to minor
flooding in a few locations.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Gaffney, Pacolet Mills, Cowpens, Mayo, Chesnee, Cowpens National
Battlefield, Thicketty, Saratt and Fingerville.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Only when it is safe to do so, please report flooding or landslides
threatening roads or property to the National Weather Service
Greenville-Spartanburg by calling 1...800...2 6 7...8 1 0 1, by
posting on our Facebook page, or by posting on X using hashtag
NWSGSP. Your message should describe the specific location, address,
or intersection where impacts occurred and the depth of flooding
observed.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued July 25 at 8:00PM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:

...The Flood Warning is cancelled for the following rivers in
Texas...

Frio River At Tilden affecting Live Oak and McMullen Counties.

For the Nueces River...including Cotulla, Tilden, Three Rivers,
Mathis, Bluntzer, Calallen...Major flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Three Rivers.

* WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 40.0 feet, Significant flooding reaches miles from the
main channel, flooding homes in the flood plain near Three Rivers
to Lake Corpus Christi. Up to 4 feet of water is in River Creek
Acres Subdivision, flooding several homes. Kellner Camp along
County Road 336 floods, with water several feet deep surrounding
homes. Antelope Lane is flooded cutting off access to J.I. Hailey
Subdivision at Jones River bend. Water approaches the base of homes
along the river in Buckeye Knoll Subdivision, 2 miles west of
Swinny Switch.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:15 PM CDT Saturday the stage was 1.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 20.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage
Tuesday afternoon and continue rising to 40.2 feet Thursday
evening. Additional rises are possible thereafter.
- Flood stage is 25.0 feet.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued July 25 at 8:44PM EDT until July 26 at 4:10PM EDT by NWS Peachtree City GA
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Georgia...

Big Creek near Alpharetta affecting Fulton and Forsyth Counties.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Big Creek near Alpharetta.

* WHEN...Until Sunday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 8.0 feet, Minor flooding continues to expand further
into the woodlands and fields along the creek from near Cumming in
south Forsyth County to Alpharetta and Roswell in north Fulton
County. Additional portions of The Big Creek Greenway have minor
flooding with 1 to 2 feet of water. Most of the walking and biking
paths will be closed...especially upstream and downstream from the
gage on Kimball Bridge Road and near Rock Mill Park. Portions of
the YMCA Campground off Preston Ridge Road will flood.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:45 PM EDT Saturday the stage was 8.4 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:45 PM EDT Saturday was 9.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage by
Sunday afternoon and continue to slowly fall through Monday.
- Flood stage is 7.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 8.4
feet on 01/20/2001.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: Air Quality Alert issued July 24 at 4:56PM MDT by NWS Missoula MT
properties.description:
AQAMSO

* WHAT...Air Quality Advisory due to smoke from wildfires.

Air Quality Index ranging from Moderate to Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups.

* WHERE...All Areas on the Nez Perce Reservation.

* WHEN...Until 10:00 AM PDT Monday July 27.

* IMPACTS...Those who experience health effects from smoke include
children under 18, elders, pregnant women, people with asthma
or have difficulty breathing, diabetes, heart problems or
otherwise compromised health, and people who have high exposure
(those who work, exercise, or spend extensive time outdoors).
properties.instruction:
Under the most severe pollution level, sensitive groups should avoid
outdoor exposure and limit indoor activities, and everyone should
restrict their outdoor activities.

Idaho Department of Health and Welfare
https://healthandwelfare.idaho.gov/health-wellness/environmental-
health/wildfire-smoke
Idaho Smoke Information Hotline: 1-800-345-1007
